title: One switch, three Wi-Fi bands: a 1-bit polarisation-rotating RIS cell (simulation study)
description:
In plain words. Wi-Fi often has dead zones. A reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) is a flat panel of small cells that can each flip the radio wave they reflect; the right pattern of flips steers Wi-Fi into the dead zone, with no radio or amplifier of its own. A known problem is that a cell's flip drifts between the 2.4, 5 and 6 GHz Wi-Fi bands, so a pattern that works in one band fails in another. We designed, on a computer, one 15 mm cell whose single on/off setting serves 2.4 GHz and the whole 5.15-7.125 GHz span. It meets a 2 dB loss budget at every simulated angle except one, and the strict target for the flip is met only straight on, with typical parts, in the 5-7 GHz band. This is a simulation study: nothing has been built or measured.

The idea in one picture. a stadium card stunt. Each person holds a card with a different colour on each side, and together the flips make a picture. Here each cell has two states, and the pattern of states shapes where the reflected wave goes. Where the picture breaks. the cards only need to look right at one moment, while a radio cell must flip the wave the same way at every frequency it serves, and that is the hard part.

For specialists. Simulation study (Palace full-wave FEM + exact network algebra; nothing built or measured) of one 15 mm, 1-bit, polarisation-rotating reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) cell whose single shared switch state covers the 2.4-2.4835 GHz and 5.15-7.125 GHz Wi-Fi bands. Four PIN diodes, each in series with a 0201 chip inductor, on one copper layer over an air spacer, with a raised ground boss and short via that suppress an oblique-incidence centre-charging resonance. Worst-case loss over a realistic parts box (diode spread, inductor tolerance, 0.013-0.017 pF mounting capacitance) is 0.81-0.91 dB at normal incidence and at most 1.37 dB to 45 deg along the cell edges and 30 deg along the diagonal; 45 deg along the diagonal misses 2 dB (2.21 / 2.28 dB). The 180 +- 20 deg bit target is met only at normal incidence with typical parts in 5-7 GHz; the report explains why (mounting capacitance, a non-Foster requirement, the diagonal sheet-scaling limit) and gives a lower-capacitance diode option. The tables and every computed number are regenerated by the included scripts from the included network files; vendor files are not redistributed. Design, text, figures and data: CC BY 4.0; code: MIT (LICENSE-CODE).

Links. Repository, with a plain-language guide: github.com/Hashirama1337s/moki-julio-wifi-ris-cell. All projects: the Moki & Julio lab map.
